concept_summary: A reverse-loop game in the world of Fenceline: claim territory by closing a fence the enemy cannot flood past: you begin holding everything the source hands out and win by giving it all back. Where the source loop is 'Close a fence loop around open ground; every cell the enemy's flood fill cannot reach is claimed as territory, and the claim target rises each level.', here every move relinquishes ground instead of claiming it, so the map empties and the score falls. Hoarding triggers the lose state; the end screen celebrates an empty board.
first_experiment: Paper prototype: ten tokens stand in for everything the player owns and each turn must discard at least one; test with five players whether emptying the board feels like winning after three rounds.
source_idea_title: Fenceline: claim territory by closing a fence the enemy cannot flood past
why_it_is_opposite: While the source rewards accumulation (Close a fence loop around open ground; every cell the enemy's flood fill cannot reach is claimed as territory, and the claim target rises each level.), this concept rewards the opposite: progress means having less, so a winning run here would score zero in the source.

concept_summary: The fantasy of Lantern Duet: your recorded path replays and lights the bridges replanted on one shared map where every player acts at once and every move is visible. Resources, storms, and scarcities hit everyone simultaneously, so private optimization loses to public negotiation. The game only functions above fifty concurrent players.
first_experiment: Moderated crowd test: put fifteen volunteers on one shared board for twenty minutes; if alliances form without prompting, the social layer carries the game.
source_idea_title: Lantern Duet: your recorded path replays and lights the bridges
why_it_is_opposite: While the source is a private experience, this concept flips it into a crowd: playing alone is impossible here, whereas the source never requires another person.

concept_summary: The same core loop as SKYHOP: play starts at page load and every run ends with your best line replayed, rebuilt end to end for newcomers instead of its current crowd. Controls, difficulty, session shape, and rewards assume newcomers: a guided, jargon-free on-ramp for total beginners. Nothing in this build serves the old crowd; one client cannot satisfy both.
first_experiment: Take one level from the source fantasy, apply the inverted tuning only, and playtest with five target players for ten minutes; a quit-rate on the opposite side of half from the source baseline confirms the audience split is real.
source_idea_title: SKYHOP: play starts at page load and every run ends with your best line replayed
why_it_is_opposite: While the source is tuned for its current crowd (Instant-play arcade players arriving from a feed with no patience for a menu.: systems tuned for veterans of the genre), this concept flips every tuning decision toward newcomers (a guided, jargon-free on-ramp for total beginners), so the two builds want mutually exclusive players.
